data.narrative:
Quaise Energy is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Carlos Araque and Matthew Houde that has raised $134M to date. The valuation comp universe in Climate & Energy includes one public company (LNZA) and eight private peers, though a narrow peer set meeting stage and valuation-tier criteria was unavailable for direct median benchmarking.

Given the limited peer overlap, the primary applicable method is stage-progression analysis. Using total capital raised of $134M as a valuation proxy and applying a typical Series A-to-next-stage step-up multiplier of 2.0x yields an implied valuation of $268M. This single-method triangulation is supported by a sensitivity range of $228M (low) to $308M (high), reflecting ±15% variance around the median point.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $228M to $308M, with $268M as the central case. Key uncertainties stem from the absence of tightly comparable private-market pricing in the Climate & Energy sector at Quaise's stage. The inference relies heavily on stage-progression convention rather than peer-observed outcomes. Any refinement would require either identification of additional same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables in deep geothermal or related thermal energy technologies, or downstream financing milestones that would anchor market-based valuation signals.
